speaker: Abu Noor
text: So. Ten at night, and I was still in Baghdad.

speaker: Guest, then Abu Noor
text: And then you died? / No. That is not how it went.

speaker: Child, then Abu Noor
text: Then how are you HERE? / ...Good question. Again.

speaker: Driver
text: Fourth gear! Tell them about fourth gear!

speaker: Uncle
text: All night? At your age? In that car?

speaker: Aunt
text: Drink your tea before it goes cold.

speaker: Old woman
text: God keep you, my son. Not so fast.

speaker: Old woman
text: Eat, my son. A thin man should not drive at night.

speaker: Old woman
text: Give it here. Straight. Like this.

speaker: Old woman
text: O Protector. O Protector. O Protector.

speaker: Soldier
text: Wake me at the checkpoint. Not before.

speaker: Soldier
text: Take one. They are the army's.

speaker: Soldier
text: What? I am awake. I was awake.

speaker: Drummer
text: Mind the drum. It is worth more than the car.

speaker: Student
text: Basra? I can pay. A little.

speaker: Student
text: I have it. He says ten, for the airport.

speaker: Student
text: Your wife, uncle. She asks if you have eaten.

speaker: Boy
text: My master says a car like this should not still be running.

speaker: Boy
text: I have the wheel. Three seconds.

speaker: Boy
text: Don't touch the lever. I am in there.

speaker: Newsreader
text: Traffic police are out on the southern road tonight.

speaker: Noor, then Abu Noor
text: They say one hand doesn't clap. / No. But it drives.

speaker: Abu Noor
text: You want the whole night? Then pour the tea and sit down, because this road has more turns in it than all of your uncle's stories put together.
Blessed: the next scrape lights no lamp
(his phone rings in his pocket: Noor)
The street: %s m to the bay
In the bay: turn the key
(he is searched: out of the car, everything open)
(he is sent to the back of the queue)
(the notes are gone; he is waved on)
Checkpoint: the soldier is %s s away

speaker: Child
text: And a truck full of MELONS! And they all fell off!

speaker: Child
text: Both hands! You have to drive with BOTH hands!

speaker: Driver
text: Tell them how close you cut it. Three of them, one after the other!

speaker: Driver
text: And on the straight you let go of the wheel. Go on, tell them!

speaker: Driver
text: You passed three of them before I could count to ten!

speaker: Uncle
text: With one hand. On that road. And we are to believe it.

speaker: In-law
text: And you stayed calm, of course? The whole way?

speaker: In-law
text: You are not one of those drivers who lean on the horn, are you?

speaker: Aunt
text: Eat something. You never eat. Have some seeds.

speaker: Aunt
text: That window! You will catch your death. Wind it.

speaker: Aunt
text: Look at the state of that glass. Wipe it.

speaker: Groom
text: They say that car has a fourth gear, uncle. I have never seen it.

speaker: Groom
text: I would have passed them. Three, at least.

speaker: Groom
text: Forgive me, uncle. But were you not afraid?

speaker: Groom
text: You are shaking, uncle. Light one. Please.

speaker: Groom
text: Sound the horn for us, uncle. For the wedding.

speaker: Old woman
text: He was gentle as a lamb, this one. Were you not, my son?

speaker: Old woman
text: Drink, my son. I told him then and I tell him now.

speaker: Soldier
text: He drove like my sergeant was behind us. That close. Three times!

speaker: Soldier
text: I slept through most of it. Was it really so hard?

speaker: Drummer
text: There was a wedding on the road that night too! I played for them from the window!

speaker: Drummer
text: He kept time on the wheel with me. No hands!

speaker: Student
text: And then it rained. I remember: my notes were ruined.

speaker: Student
text: He never once raised his voice. Or the horn. Is that not so?

speaker: Boy
text: We passed everybody, ustadh! Three at a time!

speaker: Boy
text: The wipers, ustadh! Show them how you do the wipers!
A ghost left hand is on the wheel
